{"files": [{"content": "# Blackout

Think it through without looking at a screen.

You state a goal, press Lights off, and think out loud while the screen stays black. Blackout listens, stays quiet by default, and returns a cited summary, a mind map, decisions, todos, and a hand-drawn picture when you finish.

![How Blackout works](app/static/how_it_works_en.jpg)

Demo video: https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think/releases/download/v1.0/blackout_demo.mp4 · Replay with no key and no install: https://huangfe9.github.io/blackout-think/app/static/example.html

## What it does

- You type or speak a goal and press Lights off. The screen goes pure black.
- You think out loud. No key presses are needed.
- It stays quiet and builds a mind map from what you say.
- When you drift off the goal, it parks the idea and brings you back in one sentence.
- If you say "please look up...", it searches in the background and reports back in one spoken sentence.
- If a fact you stated changes, it asks which version holds.
- After a long quiet stretch, it gives one short status line.
- Say "Stop" and the light comes on. The summary is read aloud.
- If anything goes wrong, it says so out loud.
- A second window, the star map, shows the mind map growing. It is for a second screen or a video.
- It works in English and Chinese.

## What you get

![Sample result page](app/static/sample/en.jpg)

This is real output from a fictional talk, not a mock-up. You get a short summary, a clean mind map, decisions, todos, open questions, parked ideas, contradictions, and unfinished points. Every summary item can be opened to show the exact words it came from. If you said you needed to write something, a first draft is included. A one-page hand-drawn picture is drawn from the checked summary.

## Run it

You need Python 3.10 or newer, Chrome or Edge, a microphone, and your own Meta Model API key from https://dev.meta.ai/api-keys/ .

```bash
git clone https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think
cd blackout-think
pip install -r requirements.txt
python start.py
```

A browser opens and asks for your key. A key in `.env` or in the environment also works. See `.env.example`.

Run the tests with `python -m pytest`. No key or network is needed for the tests.

## Your key and your words

- The key is saved in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blackout\api_key` on Windows or `~/.blackout/api_key` elsewhere, outside the repository.
- It gets owner-only permissions where the system supports them. Anyone with access to your computer user account can still read the file, as with any local credential.
- The key is checked with Meta before it is saved. It is sent only to `api.meta.ai`.
- No route returns the key, not even masked. The browser does not keep it. Logs redact it.
- Only the computer running the server can set, change, or delete it, and only from the app's own page.
- Use a key with a spending limit set in Meta's billing page if you can.
- Paid calls come from your own Meta account. They stop at `BLACKOUT_STOP_AT_USD`, default $10 and at most $140, enforced locally by `budget.py`.
- A short talk of about 25 sentences costs about $0.20, including the search, the draft, and the picture. A longer talk costs more in proportion.
- Speech and text go only to the Meta Model API. Sessions are saved on your own computer and can be deleted from the past sessions list.
- There are no accounts. Nothing is sent to the author.

## How it differs from a voice assistant

- Silence is the default. Most turns get no reply, only a quiet tick.
- It tracks the whole line of thought against your goal, not one question at a time.
- Drift is parked, not followed into a new conversation.
- It ends with one page whose items trace back to your exact words.

## Measured behaviour

These numbers are from `docs/evals.md`, run 2026-11-02 on the final code. They are fictional talks typed through the same code path as real speech, skipping only speech recognition. Simple rules scored them. They measure behaviour, not whether the product helps people.

8 fictional talks, 124 lines in total. The AI spoke on 31 lines and made 0 unasked interruptions. Pull-backs: 8 of 8. Changed facts asked about: 7 of 8. Look-ups started: 8 of 8. Decisions found: 8 of 10. Todos: 8 of 8. Open questions: 6 of 8. Parked items: 8 of 8. Both talks that called for a draft got one, and 4 other talks with a writing todo also got an unasked draft. Median turn was about 4.2 seconds. Average cost was $0.12 per talk of 15 to 17 lines, including search and draft, with no picture. A picture adds $0.01 plus a short check.

Real paid evaluations can be run with `python -m tests.evals.run_evals`. The normal test suite makes no paid calls.

## How it uses Meta models

- `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` hears you. It runs over a realtime connection in hands-free mode, and transcribes uploaded audio for the push-to-talk fallback and goal dictation.
- `muse-spark-1.3` runs each turn. It returns a strict structured decision and additions to the mind map.
- `muse-spark-1.3` with `web_search` does background look-ups. Without tools, it writes background drafts and reads photos of paper sketches.
- `muse-spark-1.3` does the final pass. It reads every utterance and returns the summary, the clean mind map, decisions, todos, and open questions, each citing the utterances it came from.
- `muse-image-1.0` draws the one-page hand-drawn picture from the checked summary. One picture costs $0.01.
- `muse-spark-1.3` then reads the picture back to check its text. Text in a picture can still come out wrong. The picture can be redrawn.
- Only Spark, Voice, and Image run in the product. See "Contributors and how this was built" for the models that generated the code.

## How it works

- `app/conductor.py` decides each turn: listen, follow up, pull back, answer, or start background work. Silence is the default.
- `app/realtime.py` bridges the browser microphone to the realtime speech API and separates the AI's echo from real speech by comparing text.
- `app/summary.py` runs the final pass and drops any item whose citations do not match a numbered utterance.
- `app/poster.py` plans the picture, asks `muse-image-1.0` to draw it, and has Spark read it back to check the text.
- `app/keys.py` saves, checks, and redacts the API key. No route returns it.
- `budget.py` is the local hard spending limit. It records each paid call and refuses calls past the cap.
- There are no accounts. A browser owns its sessions through a cookie, and only a hash of that cookie is stored.
- Sessions are one JSON file each on your computer, saved after every turn.

## On a phone

Run `python -m app.phone` and open the printed address on a phone on the same Wi-Fi. It serves HTTPS with a self-signed certificate and an access token, because phones need HTTPS for the microphone. The phone will warn about the certificate once. This has not yet been tried on a physical phone.

## Limits

- It needs a quiet-enough place to talk aloud.
- It has not been tried by anyone except the author. No effectiveness claims are made.
- It is a thinking tool, not a treatment for attention problems. It gives no health advice.
- The end-to-end browser flow has been run on Windows with Chrome. macOS and Linux run the automated tests in CI only.
- A physical phone has not been tested.
- Speech output uses the browser's voice. Quality varies by device.
- Text in a generated picture can still come out wrong despite the check. It can be redrawn.
- It is not built for public hosting. That would need per-visitor spending limits and data expiry.
- Multiple speakers are not told apart.
- Clearing browser cookies loses access to past sessions, because there are no accounts.

## Contributors and how this was built

Only human contributor: huangfe9 (GitHub), who had the idea, made the product decisions, and tried it.

Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, through the Meta Model API, generated the code, tests, and docs. Of these, only `muse-spark-1.3` is also used by the running product, along with `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` and `muse-image-1.0`. `muse-wonder-1.0` is not used at run time. Raw model output is in `muse_runs/` and the prompts are in `spec/`.

Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent) drafted the prompts from the author's idea, ran the generation, reviewed and tested the output, wrote throwaway test scripts that are not in this repository, assembled the demo video from a real recording, and made the commits. Security reviews by Claude Code produced findings that Muse then fixed.

This public repository starts from a clean commit. Earlier development happened in a private repository during the event.

## 中文说明

Blackout 是一个不用看屏幕的思考工具。
输入今天的目标，按下关灯，屏幕变黑。
你直接说出想法，它默认安静地听，并整理成思维导图。
说偏了，它会先记下，再把你带回目标。
说"帮我查一下"，它会在后台搜索，只说一句结论。
说"结束"，灯亮起来，你会得到摘要、决定、待办和一张手绘图。
每一条都能点开，看到它来自你的哪句原话。
运行：git clone https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think，然后 cd blackout-think，pip install -r requirements.txt，python start.py。
需要你自己的 Meta Model API key，费用从你的账户扣除。

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`.

Blackout

Tagline
Think it through without looking at a screen.

Short description
Blackout lets you think out loud with the screen off. It stays quiet, tracks your points, parks drift, and returns a cited summary, mind map, decisions, todos, and a hand-drawn picture when you say Stop.

Description
Tools for thinking usually live on the same screen that distracts from thinking. Blackout removes the screen instead of reminding you to focus. You type or speak a goal, press Lights off, and the screen goes black. You think out loud, walking around, lying down, or sketching on paper, with no keys to press. The AI listens continuously and stays quiet by default, building a mind map against your goal. It speaks only when a point was left unfinished, a fact you stated has changed, you drifted off the goal, you asked it something, or you have gone silent for a long stretch. Drift is stored in a parking lot and you are brought back in one sentence. A request to look something up runs in the background while you keep talking, then reports one spoken sentence. When you say Stop, the light comes on at once. You get a summary read aloud, a clean mind map, decisions, todos, open questions, parked ideas, and a hand-drawn one-page picture. A voice assistant answers every sentence. Blackout's main behaviour is knowing when to say nothing, and tracking the whole line of thought instead of one exchange at a time.

How it uses Meta's models
Each turn, muse-spark-1.3 returns a strict structured decision: listen, follow up, pull back, continue, answer, summarise, or start background work. Listen is the default, so silence is enforced by the schema and by server rules, not left to chance. The model returns additions only, never a rewritten state, so nothing recorded can be lost. muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 runs over a realtime connection with cumulative partials. Because browser echo cancellation does not cover speechSynthesis, the server tells the AI's echo from real speech by comparing recognised text with what was just spoken, so you can talk over the AI and be heard. At the end, Spark reads every utterance and must cite numbered utterances for each summary item. The server checks the citations and drops any item without a valid one. Spark then reads back the picture drawn by muse-image-1.0 to check its text. Muse Spark and Muse Wonder also generated the project itself.

Technical highlights
- Strict structured output each turn, with additions only and a server-side rule that keeps listen turns silent.
- Realtime speech over a WebSocket bridge, with text-based echo detection so the microphone stays on while the AI speaks.
- A deterministic mind map tree built on the server from additions, shown live in the star map window and tidied by the final pass.
- Citation checking on the server: final items without a matching numbered utterance are dropped, and a later statement replaces an earlier one rather than counting as a contradiction.
- Local spend control in budget.py, owner-only key storage outside the repository, and sessions scoped to the owning browser with no accounts.

Theme and track
Theme: Build for Your World. Track: Indie developer (solo-built).

Links
Repository: https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think
Demo video: https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think/releases/download/v1.0/blackout_demo.mp4
Replay, no key and no install: https://huangfe9.github.io/blackout-think/app/static/example.html

How to try it
Open the replay link above. It needs no key and no install. To run the real app, use your own Meta Model API key from https://dev.meta.ai/api-keys/ and run: git clone https://github.com/huangfe9/blackout-think ; cd blackout-think ; pip install -r requirements.txt ; python start.py . A browser opens and asks for the key. A short talk of about 25 sentences costs about $0.20 from your own Meta account, including the search, the draft, and the picture.

Contributors
Only human contributor: huangfe9 (GitHub), who had the idea, made the product decisions, and tried it. Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, through the Meta Model API, generated the code, tests, and docs. Raw model output is in muse_runs/, prompts in spec/. Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent) drafted the prompts from the author's idea, ran the generation, reviewed and tested the output, wrote throwaway test scripts that are not in this repository, assembled the demo video from a real recording, and made the commits. Security reviews by Claude Code produced findings that Muse then fixed. This public repository starts from a clean commit, and earlier development happened in a private repository during the event. Only muse-spark-1.3, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, and muse-image-1.0 are used by the running product.

Known limits
- Not tried by anyone except the author, so no effectiveness claims are made. It needs a quiet-enough place to talk aloud, and multiple speakers are not told apart.
- The end-to-end browser flow has been run on Windows with Chrome. macOS and Linux run the automated tests in CI only, and a physical phone has not been tested.
- Speech output uses the browser's voice, whose quality varies by device. Text in a generated picture can still come out wrong despite the check, and it can be redrawn.
- Not built for public hosting: it would need per-visitor spending limits and data expiry. Clearing browser cookies loses access to past sessions.

Pre-submit checklist
- [ ] Repo is public.
- [ ] Video link works when logged out.
- [ ] Everyone who contributed is listed.
- [ ] Submitted through the Cerebral Valley platform before Nov 4, 9 PM ET.
- [ ] API credits claimed.
- [ ] Eligibility confirmed against the official rules, which exclude some countries and regions.
- [ ] The official rules checked for anything these notes missed.

The video is about 3 minutes. It follows `docs/demo_talk.json`, goal: "Decide how to run a small product launch this week".

## What the video shows

- Title: "Blackout: thinking without a screen". On screen: "Recorded live against the real Meta API. The voices are computer speech."
- Start: "Type one goal. Press Lights off." The goal is typed and Lights off is pressed.
- Black: "This black screen is all you get. From here, voice only." The screen is pure black with a dim dot.
- Open: "One goal, three things to sort out." The speaker names the launch day, support cover, and the announcement.
- Quiet: "The AI stays silent and quietly builds the map." The speaker decides Thursday morning and three people on support. The AI says nothing.
- Drift: "Off topic: the idea is parked, attention returns." The speaker wants hot pot tonight. The AI parks it and pulls back.
- Lookup: "A lookup runs in the background while thinking continues." The speaker asks when launch emails get the most opens and keeps thinking.
- Conflict: "Five, not three: the AI asks about the change." The speaker says five people on support.
- Answer: "Corrected to three, with weekend cover on-call only." The speaker settles it.
- Todo: "A writing todo the AI can draft later." A short launch email is due Wednesday.
- Open question: "An open question is kept, not answered away." Marketing review timing is unknown.
- Stop: "One word ends it and brings the light back." The speaker says "Stop."
- Wait: "Lights on at once. The real 15-second summary wait is shortened here." The result page appears at once and fills in.
- Result: "One page: summary, decisions, todos, and a picture from Muse Image."
- Words: "Every item opens to the exact words behind it." A summary item is expanded to its source sentences.
- Draft: "It noticed a writing todo and drafted it in the background." The launch email draft is shown.
- Picture: "The same picture, drawn from the checked summary." The hand-drawn picture is shown, then the closing lines: "No screen while you think. One page when you finish." and "It runs on your own computer with your own Meta key."

The star map window is visible beside the black screen, so viewers can see the mind map growing while the speaker cannot.

## How it was made

- This was a real run, not a mock-up. A computer voice speaks the lines in `docs/demo_talk.json` into the app's microphone input.
- The app called the real Meta API during the recording. The speaker and the AI are both computer voices.
- The screen was captured and edited. The summary wait was shortened, and the video says so on screen.
- No lines, replies, or results were typed in by hand for the recording.

## How to re-record it with your own voice

- Run the app with your own key: `python start.py`. Keep the key page out of the recording.
- Tick the option to open the star map window, so the map is visible on screen.
- Read the same lines from `docs/demo_talk.json` in order, with the pauses marked there. Speak the end phrase last.
- Record with any screen recorder. Keep the black screen, the star map, and the result page in frame.
- If you shorten the summary wait in editing, say so on screen, as this video does.
